statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail 6% (low), Stress 48% (elevated), Confidence 89% (high), dominant mode normal. The overnight round trip has retraced and NQZ26 has reclaimed the 31,061.75 prior close with a higher low and a higher high.
recommendation: Tail at 6% remains well below the 25% block threshold, so the deterministic mapping yields EA_ON and green for both NQ futures and the NAS100 CFD. The narrow evidence-based danger window spans 13:00Z to 15:00Z, covering the 13:30Z US cash open, the 13:45Z S&P Global September finals and the 14:00Z September ISM Services release. Stress at 48% stays elevated and describes a difficult but recoverable high-yield environment; it does not alter the Tail-derived mapping.
headline: Tail eases to 6% as NQZ26 reclaims the 31,061.75 prior close with a higher low and a higher high, completing the retracement of the 217.5-point overnight round trip, while Stress falls to 48% on WTI below 90 and the 10Y easing from Friday's 5.28%
body:
An hour ago the evidence said a three-hour lower-low sequence had stopped and price was compressing in a 17.5-point band. The 08:00Z hour answers what the compression resolved into, and it resolved upward. NQZ26 prints 31,077.25 at 08:21:57Z against the 31,061.75 prior close, up 15.50 points or 0.050%. The hour traded 31,045.75 to 31,099.25. The 07:00Z hour traded 31,022.75 to 31,072.75. Both the low and the high are higher, which is the first unambiguous higher low plus higher high of the overnight, and the prior close has been reclaimed for the first time since the decline started.

The structure of what was retraced matters as much as the retracement. From the 31,221.25 high printed in the 01:00Z hour, price fell to 31,003.75 at 06:40Z: 217.5 points, 0.70%, across roughly five and three-quarter hours. That is under 40 points an hour, each hourly low was bought, and the largest single hourly range inside the decline was 102 points at 02:00Z. There was no gap, no repeated extension after a failed retracement, and no session-extreme holding. The decline was a slow drift, and the recovery has been faster than the decline: 95.5 points at the 08:16Z high against 217.5 points lost over nearly six hours, with one hour and forty-one minutes elapsed since the low with no new low.

Under the risk contract this is the signature of mean reversion working. Tail measures the probability that mean reversion fails long enough to create a persistent one-way path. A completed 217.5-point round trip that then reverses through its reference close is the direct opposite of that, and the contract permits Tail to fall quickly once an orderly retracement has actually occurred. Tail therefore eases from 9% to 6%, mapping deterministically to EA_ON and green for both NQ futures and the NAS100 CFD, with the dominant mode normal. It is not taken lower than 6% because a live, scoreable price path exists and the 31,221.25 high remains unretested after roughly seven hours, which leaves the overnight's directional question open rather than settled.

Cross-asset evidence supports the easing. WTI trades 89.41, down 1.87% with a 89.31 session low, and Brent 100.77, down 1.45%, continuing the slide from above 93 dollars as the verified G7 and IEA coordinated release of up to 100 million barrels of crude and diesel takes effect and Middle East crude exports recover. Treasury futures are firmer across the curve, the 2-year contract up 0.073%, the 10-year up 0.195% and the 30-year up 0.305%, consistent with the cash 10-year easing to roughly 5.26% from Friday's 5.28% close. ES at plus 0.006% and YM at plus 0.054% put the broader complex flat to marginally higher, an alignment of five basis points or less that is explicitly not an impulse. The counter-signal is VIX at 16.18, up 5.68% from 15.31; it is a genuine rise, but 16 is a historically low absolute level and generic volatility informs Stress rather than Tail under the contract.

Stress eases from 51% to 48% and remains elevated. The easing credits the oil rollover and the firmer bond complex. The level stays elevated because the regime has not changed: the 10-year sits near 24-year highs after briefly touching 5.34%, the quarter just ended produced the largest 10-year yield increase this century, the Federal Reserve hiked 25 basis points unanimously in September and still projects one further increase this year even as October odds have faded below one in four, and an active Middle East conflict persists while its oil-price transmission deflates. That is a difficult environment that can still mean-revert, which is what elevated Stress alongside low Tail is designed to express.

Confidence holds at 89%. The evidence base is continuous five-minute and one-minute Nasdaq-100 futures data to 08:21:57Z, live ES, YM, VIX, WTI, Brent, gold, dollar-index and Treasury-futures quotes, verified 10-year yield levels, the verified G7 and IEA release, the verified Federal Reserve path and a verified seven-day US calendar. It is not raised because the shared Finviz context is roughly six days stale with its futures and calendar sections unavailable and was therefore excluded from this assessment, and because cash-market breadth, megacap and semiconductor internals are only available at Friday's close with the US cash session still about five hours away.

The forward path keeps Tail between 6% and 14% across all 24 slots, so every forecast hour maps to EA_ON and green. The band peaks at the 13:00Z and 14:00Z slots for the US cash open, the 13:45Z S&P Global September finals and the 14:00Z September ISM Services release, and the danger window is held narrow at 13:00Z to 15:00Z to cover exactly that cluster. Those increments are conditional allowances for a scheduled checkpoint. No post-event structure is observed, and under the contract event importance and surprise magnitude raise Stress and inform Confidence rather than raising Tail until an actual price path establishes otherwise. The 7 October FOMC Minutes at 18:00Z remain the week's dominant scheduled catalyst and sit outside this forecast horizon.

lookbackSummary: Twenty-three of the 24 preceding published hours are available from Claude history, and every available hour mapped to EA_ON and green with the dominant mode normal. The 06:00Z slot on 5 October is explicitly unavailable because no assessment was published inside that clock-hour; its fields are null rather than interpolated. Tail was pinned at 3% from 08:00Z through 21:00Z on 4 October because the CME equity-index complex was halted for the weekend and no Nasdaq-100 price path was scoreable. It then rose through the Sunday reopen as the overnight drift extended, reaching 12% at 22:00Z, 13% at 23:00Z, 14% at 00:00Z and a 15% peak at 01:00Z on 5 October, the hour that printed the 31,221.25 overnight high. It eased to 13% at 02:00Z once that high failed, to 10% at 03:00Z, and to 8% at 04:00Z and 05:00Z as the retracement through the prior close appeared to hold. The 07:00Z hour published 9% after the three-hour lower-low sequence stopped. Stress ran a 79% ceiling at 09:00Z on 4 October and has decayed almost monotonically since, through 71% at 21:00Z, 62% at 01:00Z and 51% at 07:00Z, tracking the oil complex rolling over on the verified G7 and IEA coordinated reserve release. Confidence held a tight 83% to 89% band throughout, reflecting continuously available futures evidence rather than any change in method.

NQZ26 prints 31,077.25 at 08:21:57Z against the 31,061.75 prior close, a gain of 15.50 points or 0.050%, and the hour has traded a 31,045.75 to 31,099.25 range. Both extremes are higher than the 07:00Z hour's 31,022.75 low and 31,072.75 high, so the market has produced a higher low and a higher high and has reclaimed the prior close for the first time since the decline began. Measured from the 31,003.75 session low at 06:40Z, the recovery reached 95.5 points and stands at 73.5, with no new low in one hour and forty-one minutes. The decline it retraced was itself orderly: 217.5 points, or 0.70%, spread across roughly five and three-quarter hours from the 31,221.25 high, averaging under 40 points an hour with a bounce off every hourly low. A 217.5-point round trip that completes and reverses is mean reversion working, not failing, so Tail eases from 9% to 6% and maps to EA_ON and green with the dominant mode normal. Cross-assets corroborate rather than contradict. WTI trades 89.41, down 1.87% at a 89.31 session low, and Brent 100.77, down 1.45%, extending the decline from above 93 dollars as the G7 and IEA coordinated 100-million-barrel release takes effect and Middle East crude exports recover. Treasury futures are firmer across the curve, with the 10-year contract up 0.195% and the 30-year up 0.305%, consistent with the cash 10-year easing to about 5.26% from Friday's 5.28% close. ES at plus 0.006% and YM at plus 0.054% show the complex flat to marginally higher with no impulse. The one genuine counter-signal is VIX at 16.18, up 5.68% from 15.31, which is a rising but historically low absolute level and does not by itself establish a pathological path. Stress therefore eases to 48%, still elevated, because the structural backdrop is unchanged: the 10-year sits near 24-year highs after the largest quarterly yield rise this century, the Federal Reserve hiked in September and still projects one more increase this year, and an active Middle East conflict continues even as its oil transmission deflates. Forward Tail stays inside a 6% to 14% band for all 24 slots, so every forecast hour maps to EA_ON and green. The band peaks at the 13:00Z and 14:00Z slots, which carry the US cash open, the S&P Global September finals and September ISM Services, and the narrow danger window spans 13:00Z to 15:00Z accordingly. Those increments are conditional catalyst allowances, not assertions that post-event structure is already observed. Confidence holds at 89% on continuous fresh futures and cross-asset evidence plus a verified seven-day calendar; it is not raised further because the shared Finviz context is roughly six days stale and partial and was therefore excluded, and because cash-market internals are only available at Friday's close.
